messages:
alex_s: FYI customer Brightline reported a sudden vectors/sec drop on /v1/embeddings — tokens/sec looks stable. They saw throughput ~80% lower starting ~03:10 UTC. No 4xx/5xx, just much slower vectors. payloads are 512-dim, client batch_size=32. Can we triage?

anika: Ugh. Do we have a sample request + model id? Any recent rollout that could affect batching/queueing? :eyes:

ryan_infra: I was on pager around that time — there was a small batching-window tweak pushed at 03:05 to reduce latency for short requests. Might've reduced average batch fill and increased GPU kernel churn. Need logs for batch window fills + GPU queue depth.

maya_ml: Also check whether embeddings path fell back to a different quantization/kernel (e.g., fallback to fp16->int8 shim) when dim==512. That can change throughput a lot.

alex_s: Sample request from customer (sanitized):

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer **REDACTED**" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-512","input":["...512 tokens..."],"batch_size":32}'
```

No auth errors, billing OK. Customer says tokens/sec (measured client-side) stayed ~120k/s but vectors/sec plunged to ~8k/s (expected ~40k/s).

ops-bot: Deployment event: batching-window tweak rolled to canary at 2026-03-17T03:05:12Z by ryan_infra. Change-id: cw-20260317-03.

ryan_infra: Yep that was the change. It shortens max_batch_delay from 12ms -> 5ms for small requests. Good for p99 latency but if their traffic has low concurrency it will kill batching efficiency.

anika: Can we reproduce quickly? alex, can you run a small experiment toggling max_batch_delay back to 12ms for the customer's routing pool or run a load script to measure vectors/sec vs tokens/sec?

alex_s: Running a repro now against a mirror pool. Quick script:

```python
# simplified load runner
for i in range(1000):
  post('/v1/embeddings', json={'model':'embed-large-512','input':['...512...']*32})
```

Results after 5 min (canary config with 5ms): tokens/sec ~118k, vectors/sec ~7.9k.

Switching pool to old batch window (12ms) -> rerun...

Results with 12ms: tokens/sec ~120k, vectors/sec ~39.5k.

maya_ml: That's pretty conclusive — the shorter batch window massively reduced vectors/sec because batch fill dropped from avg 28 -> avg 6, so GPU utilization dropped and kernel launch overhead dominates.

ryan_infra: I'll roll a targeted rollback for that routing pool and schedule an operator change to make the batch-window adaptive by concurrency. For now, rollback to previous window for affected customer ID.

ops-bot: Rollback recorded: change-id cw-20260317-03 -> rolled back on pool brightline-mirror by ryan_infra at 2026-03-17T03:47:05Z.

anika: Good catch. Alex, pls communicate to Brightline what we changed, include repro artifacts (script, before/after numbers) and ask if they want the conservative config or the lower-latency config. Also open a follow-up ticket to make batch-window adaptive.

alex_s: Will do. Drafting message and attaching load runner output and batch-fill histograms. Thanks team :thumbsup:

maya_ml: Follow-up note: we should add an automated alert when vectors/sec deviates from tokens/sec by >50% for a sustained 2 minutes, to catch this earlier.

ryan_infra: Agree. Filing ops ticket now.

alex_s: Closing this thread once Brightline confirms throughput is back.
